summary: Australia is witnessing a significant maturation in its approach to animal welfare, marked by legislative innovation and community-driven care. A new Animal Welfare Commission Advisory Committee is being formed to integrate public policy with industry expertise, ensuring that legislative processes are informed by both scientific rigor and practical experience. Simultaneously, the RSPCA has advanced its 'RSPCA Certified' trademark, a move that standardizes welfare standards for farmed animals and promotes continuous improvement across the sector. These developments reflect a broader national commitment to responsible pet ownership and the protection of companion animals, supported by dedicated veterinary networks and rescue organizations.

goodNews.title: New Animal Welfare Commission Advisory Committee Formed
goodNews.angle: This initiative brings together experts in public policy, community education, and industry to advise on legislative duties, fostering a collaborative and evidence-based approach to animal welfare in Australia.

goodNews.title: RSPCA Certified Becomes a Certification Trade Mark
goodNews.angle: By establishing a recognized trade mark, the RSPCA is helping to standardize and verify welfare practices for farmed animals, promoting transparency and continuous improvement in the agricultural sector.

goodNews.title: Pets in Aged Care: 86% Report Improved Health
goodNews.angle: Data from the Companion Animal Network Australia highlights that 86% of older adults experience improved mental and physical health with pets, underscoring the vital role of companion care in supporting human well-being.

goodNews.title: Global Acceleration of Science Without Animal Testing
goodNews.angle: International scientific breakthroughs and federal actions are accelerating the transition away from animal testing, representing a major ethical and technological advancement in global research practices.
